from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Secant lines connect two points on a curve.",
            "Average change is calculated as Δy divided by Δx.",
            "A snail moves along a path between two points."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Static Concept (Secant Lines)", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in a curve on a #FFFFFF background. (Representing curve as parabola)
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B2", "E5")
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a secant line between two points on the curve (#FFD700).
        # Label the two points as x and x+h (#00BFFF).
        # Display the slope formula m = Δy/Δx clearly (#32CD32).
        p1 = curve.point_from_proportion(0.2)
        p2 = curve.point_from_proportion(0.8)
        secant = Line(p1, p2, color="#FFD700")
        
        point_a = Dot(p1, color="#00BFFF")
        point_b = Dot(p2, color="#00BFFF")
        label_a = MathTex("x", color="#00BFFF", font_size=24).next_to(point_a, DOWN)
        label_b = MathTex("x+h", color="#00BFFF", font_size=24).next_to(point_b, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(secant), FadeIn(point_a), FadeIn(point_b), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))
        
        formula = MathTex(r"m = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}", color="#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#32CD32")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the secant line segment with a glowing effect (#FF4500).
        # A snail moves along a path between two points.
        glow = secant.copy().set_stroke(color="#FF4500", width=8, opacity=0.5)
        snail = Dot(p1, color="#FF4500")
        
        self.play(Create(glow))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(snail, secant), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Transformation: The Limit Process", [
            "Let the gap between two points shrink to zero.",
            "As they converge, the secant becomes the tangent.",
            "The line snaps into the instantaneous position.",
            "This limit defines the derivative geometrically.",
            "It transforms interval change into a single point."
        ])
        
        # Setup plot area
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        func = lambda x: 0.2 * x**2 + 1
        curve = axes.plot(func, color=WHITE)
        self.add(curve)
        
        # Points
        p1 = axes.c2p(2, func(2))
        p2 = axes.c2p(4, func(4))
        dot1 = Dot(p1, color=YELLOW)
        dot2 = Dot(p2, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Secant Line
        secant = Line(p1, p2, color=YELLOW)
        self.add(dot1, dot2, secant)
        
        h = ValueTracker(2.0)
        
        def update_secant(mob):
            new_p2 = axes.c2p(2 + h.get_value(), func(2 + h.get_value()))
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(p1, new_p2)
            dot2.move_to(new_p2)
            
        secant.add_updater(update_secant)
        
        limit_text = MathTex(r"\lim_{h \to 0}", font_size=36, color="#00BFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(limit_text, "B1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(h.animate.set_value(0.1), run_time=3)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        secant.remove_updater(update_secant)
        secant.set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(FadeOut(dot2), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00BFFF")
        self.play(Write(limit_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivatives provide a local linear approximation.",
            "Zooming in reveals the curve's linear nature.",
            "Complexity simplifies into a local straight line.",
            "This mapping captures slope at one point.",
            "The derivative is essentially local linearization."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conceptual Core: The Derivative as a Local Linearization", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Math objects
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        point = Dot(curve.point_from_proportion(0.5), color=YELLOW)
        tangent = Line(start=point.get_center() - np.array([1, 1, 0]), end=point.get_center() + np.array([1, 1, 0]), color=YELLOW)
        formula = MathTex(r"y = f(a) + f'(a)(x-a)", font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.place_at_grid(point, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.place_at_grid(tangent, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(tangent))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        zoom_view = VGroup(curve.copy(), point.copy()).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(zoom_view, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(zoom_view))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00BFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Indicate(tangent))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        formula.set_color_by_tex("f'(a)", "#32CD32")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula, formula))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Position graphs transform into velocity graphs.",
            "The derivative measures instantaneous growth factors.",
            "A cheetah's speed is the curve's steepness.",
            "The slope represents speed at a micro-second.",
            "Physics relies on these dynamic rates."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Dynamic Application: Rate of Change", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 6, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        func = lambda t: 0.2 * t**2
        graph = axes.plot(func, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Initial state
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        dot = Dot(color=ORANGE).move_to(axes.c2p(3, func(3)))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        tangent_line = TangentLine(graph, alpha=0.5, length=2, color=RED)
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        slope_label = MathTex("m = f'(t)").next_to(tangent_line, UP)
        self.play(Write(slope_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", [
            "Derivatives transform global behavior into local rates.",
            "Instantaneous slopes predict future system states.",
            "Modern technology relies on this transformation."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.1 * x**3, x_range=[-3, 3], color=WHITE)
        line = Line(start=np.array([-1, -0.1, 0]), end=np.array([1, 0.1, 0]), color=YELLOW)
        formula = MathTex(r"f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}", font_size=36)
        
        self.place_in_area(curve, "A1", "C6")
        self.place_at_grid(line, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "F3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(curve), Create(line), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.play(line.animate.rotate(0.3), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Dynamic Rates
outline.target_audience: University students (Calculus I or Physics I)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Static Concept (Secant Lines)
sections.content: Briefly revisit the idea of a secant line connecting two points on a curve. Establish the average rate of change formula: Δy/Δx. Use a visual of a line segment connecting points A and B on a parabola.
sections.example: A snail crawling from leaf A to leaf B. We calculate the average speed based on the straight path between them.

sections.title: The Transformation: The Limit Process
sections.content: Introduce the 'Transformational' view—let the distance between point A and B shrink to zero. As B approaches A, the secant line transforms into the tangent line. This is the visual 'snap' from an interval to an instantaneous point.
sections.example: Animation: A strobe light effect where the second point moves closer to the first until the line 'locks' into the tangent position.

sections.title: Conceptual Core: The Derivative as a Local Linearization
sections.content: Explain that the derivative is the 'local linear approximation' of a function. Even complex curves look like straight lines if you zoom in enough. This mapping from a curve to a slope at a single point is the core transformation.
sections.example: Zooming into a roller coaster track until the small section under the cart looks perfectly flat.

sections.title: Dynamic Application: Rate of Change
sections.content: Shift from geometry to physics. The derivative transforms a position-time graph into a velocity-time graph. Emphasize that the derivative isn't just a number; it is the 'growth factor' of the function at that exact moment.
sections.example: A cheetah accelerating: The steepness of the position curve at 't=2 seconds' represents the exact speed the cheetah hits at that micro-second.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Derivative = Transformation from a 'Global Behavior' (the whole curve) to a 'Local Capability' (the instantaneous slope/rate). This allows us to predict the future state of a system based on its current rate of change.
sections.example: A smart rocket navigation system that uses the instantaneous derivative to adjust its trajectory mid-flight.
